question: Which Linux companion app direction should this issue track now that Windows Hub has shipped: the C/GTK implementation, the Rust/GTK implementation, or a different split milestone plan?
rationale: Current main only resolves the Windows half; the Linux half has multiple active large PRs with different language, packaging, and security tradeoffs that automation should not choose.

options.title: Select one Linux architecture
options.body: Pick one Linux companion implementation as the canonical path and close or redirect competing tracks after preserving useful review context.

options.title: Split by milestone
options.body: Keep this umbrella open but create narrower Linux milestones for runtime bootstrap, tray/service integration, packaging, and node capabilities before selecting final UI scope.

options.title: Defer first-party Linux app
options.body: Keep Linux as CLI/Gateway-only for now and redirect companion app experiments outside core until maintainers are ready for a supported desktop surface.

recommendation.title: Select one Linux architecture
recommendation.body: Pick one Linux companion implementation as the canonical path and close or redirect competing tracks after preserving useful review context.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion contains steipete's product-direction comments, and the remaining choice is primarily platform direction rather than a narrow code defect.
